A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FeuN/FeuQ two-component system represents a paradigmatic example of a two-component system that integrates multiple environmental signals to control a single target gene.
FeuPQ is a two component system that responds to the periplasm and the extracellular environment.
FeuN is an extracellular signal transducer that controls the phosphorylation activity of FeuQ by a mechanism involving direct protein–protein interaction between the two proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the periplamic interaction between FeuP and FeuN introduces an intracellular change in FeuP that increases its ability to remove phosphates from its cognate sensor kinase.
